summary: Author-v1 checkpoint: the generic temperedness theorem and conditional nongeneric weight constraints are separated from their local representation-theoretic inputs. Existing Satake, excursions, weights and highest-weight suppliers are imported. The final-version comparison, complete prerequisite audit, detailed exceptional computations and exhaustive itemization remain open.

items.name: Nonzero sl2 triple
items.statement: Over a commutative ring R and an R-Lie algebra L, a triple (h,e,f) satisfies h != 0, [e,f]=h, [h,e]=2e, [h,f]=-2f.
items.note: Pinned Sl2.lean lines 35-49 read. The paper also requires the zero orbit; this library item does not cover it.

items.name: Zero-orbit comparison
items.statement: In characteristic zero, extend the nonzero-triple interface by the zero triple and prove that h=0 forces e=f=0; its filtration is concentrated in weight zero.

items.name: Jacobson-Morozov existence
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, every nilpotent e occurs in a triple satisfying the sl2 relations, allowing the zero triple.

items.name: Triples and nilpotent orbits
items.statement: In the same setting, taking the raising element induces a bijection between adjoint-conjugacy classes of triples and nilpotent orbits.

items.name: Tensor-compatible triple filtration
items.statement: For each finite-dimensional representation V, use the integral h-eigenspace decomposition to define Fil_i(V) as the sum of eigenspaces of weights at most i. Construct the functor on intertwiners and its tensor, dual and underlying-vector-space comparisons.

items.name: Recognition from every representation
items.statement: For two triples in a simple characteristic-zero Lie algebra, equality of dim Fil_i(V) for every finite-dimensional Lie representation V and every integer i implies conjugacy of the triples.
items.note: All representations, not just the standard or adjoint representation. Very-even orthogonal orbits require a half-spin separator.

items.name: Integral spectrum of a triple
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional characteristic-zero sl2-module, h is diagonalizable with integer eigenvalues after classification and complete reducibility. Treat the zero triple separately.

items.name: Integer Weil weights
items.statement: For q>1 and a nonzero algebraic number a, weight w in Z means that every complex embedding has absolute value q^(w/2). Algebraic integrality is a separate predicate.

items.name: Geometric local parameter
items.statement: For F=k((t)), ell != char(k), a semisimple ell-adic L-parameter is geometric when Frobenius eigenvalues in a faithful algebraic realization are algebraic Weil q-numbers of integer weights; prove independence of faithful realization and Frobenius lift under the source hypotheses.

items.name: Pure Weil-Deligne representation
items.statement: For a Weil-Deligne pair (phi,N) with integral Frobenius weights, use the increasing weight filtration W. Purity of weight w requires N^i:gr_(w-i) -> gr_(w+i) to be isomorphisms in the paper convention, together with the Weil-Deligne relation.
items.note: Import the local monodromy and purity interface of DWP.5. A comparison of arithmetic/geometric Frobenius and the sign convention for N remains an application-specific obligation, not a duplicate carrier.

items.name: Functorial mixed weight filtration
items.statement: For a lisse mixed rational ell-adic sheaf with integral weights, construct the unique functorial strict weight filtration with pure graded pieces. Purity does not assert arithmetic semisimplicity.

items.name: One geometric boundary place
items.statement: Let U be an open of a smooth proper curve over a finite field and L a lisse ell-adic local system. Under Proposition 2.7's geometric local representation hypothesis at u outside U, all unramified fibers have integral Weil weights.

items.name: Purity of the boundary graded pieces
items.statement: Under the preceding curve and geometricity hypotheses, the local Weil-Deligne representation at u of each weight-i graded piece is pure of weight i.
items.note: Apply DWP.5 to the pure graded pieces supplied by DWP.8; this is curve weight-monodromy, not a mixed-characteristic conjecture.

items.name: Finite-level cuspidal finiteness
items.statement: For semisimple G over the global function field and compact level U, the E-valued cuspidal automorphic forms form a finite E-module when E is a noetherian Z[1/p]-algebra embedded in the chosen algebraically closed coefficient field.

items.name: Cuspidal scalar extension
items.statement: With the hypotheses of Proposition 3.1, extension from E to the chosen algebraically closed coefficient field commutes with the space of finite-level cuspidal forms.

items.name: Algebraic cuspidal Hecke eigenvalues
items.statement: The unramified Hecke eigenvalues on the finite-level cuspidal space are algebraic numbers; keep the finite-module and coefficient-model inputs explicit.

items.name: Cuspidal excursion decomposition
items.statement: At fixed level, construct the commutative excursion algebra, its generalized-eigenspace decomposition of cusp forms, and the corresponding continuous semisimple global L-parameters. Do not impose uniqueness from the Hecke eigencharacter alone.

items.name: Unramified Frobenius compatibility
items.statement: For a parameter appearing in the cuspidal excursion decomposition, its unramified Frobenius class equals the local Satake class of the associated Hecke character, with coefficient-embedding and normalization comparisons.

items.name: Semisimple local-global comparison
items.statement: Restriction of a cuspidal global parameter to a local Weil group, followed by semisimplification, depends only on the local representation and agrees with the stated local assignment. This is not full Weil-Deligne compatibility.

items.name: Normalized local induction and Jacquet functors
items.statement: For a reductive group over a nonarchimedean local field, construct normalized parabolic induction and Jacquet functors with the chosen square root of the modulus character and valid coefficient hypotheses.

items.name: Geometric representation
items.statement: A smooth irreducible local representation defined over a number field is geometric when its semisimple local parameter is geometric in Definition 2.5. The coefficient model and embedding comparisons are part of the definition/API.

items.name: Geometric discrete series
items.statement: A discrete-series representation with geometric central character is geometric. For semisimple G the central-character condition is automatic in the source application.
items.note: Requires the actual local-parameter theorem; this is not ordinary smooth representation theory alone.

items.name: Temperedness after an embedding
items.statement: For a Qbar-model and an embedding iota:Qbar -> C, iota-temperedness means temperedness of scalar extension along iota. Absolute temperedness requires every such embedding.

items.name: Galois conjugation of discrete series
items.statement: For the semisimple local groups in Section 4.1, discrete series admit number-field models and their conjugates remain discrete series. Do not generalize to arbitrary reductive groups with unrestricted transcendental unitary central character.
items.note: The v1 text supplies a sketch and refers to a fuller proof elsewhere; proof-interior audit remains open.

items.name: Embedding independence in the cuspidal application
items.statement: For a number-field model of a cuspidal global representation as in Theorem 4.3, a local component that is tempered after one complex embedding is tempered after every complex embedding.

items.name: Aubert-Zelevinsky semisimple compatibility
items.statement: For the tempered local representations of Proposition 4.5, the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution preserves supercuspidal support and hence the semisimple local parameter. No equality of monodromy operators is asserted.

items.name: Spherical parameter dictionary
items.statement: For unramified G and a hyperspecial K, identify irreducible K-spherical representations with the appropriate relative-Weyl orbits of unramified parameters; retain Frobenius action and q-half normalization.

items.name: Tempered spherical real part
items.statement: Write a spherical Satake parameter as a compact part times q^nu, with dominant real nu. In the source unramified setting the spherical representation is tempered exactly when nu=0.

items.name: Weight classes and constant-field twists
items.statement: For the semisimple local systems tau composed with sigma in Section 5, decompose into constant-field character twists of systems with integral weights, retaining the character equivalence relation and the uniqueness asserted in (5.5).
items.note: Use DWP.8 and GLn purity; do not infer integer weights directly from real iota-weights.

items.name: Lifting the dual-group parameter
items.statement: In the nonadjoint C/D cases of Section 5, restrict the Galois parameter to a suitable finite extension to obtain the required central-isogeny lift and minuscule realizations. Construct the cover and track Frobenius powers and residue cardinalities.
items.locator: arXiv:2311.15300v1, Proof of Theorem 5.4, nonadjoint reduction
items.note: This is parameter restriction, not an assumed cuspidal automorphic base-change theorem.

items.name: Half-integrality in a representation
items.statement: A real parameter nu is half-integral in V when <lambda,nu> belongs to (1/2)Z for every weight lambda of V. This is a condition on the real part, not algebraicity of the compact Satake factor.

items.name: Generic spherical unitary region
items.statement: For split quasi-simple adjoint G, let U0 consist of dominant real parameters whose spherical quotient is both generic and unitary. Keep Hermitian symmetry w0(nu)=-nu and reducibility walls separate.

items.name: Exclusion at nonzero integral root values
items.statement: For a parameter in the real generic spherical unitary region, no positive coroot pairing is a positive integer. A pair on the reducibility wall is not an interior generic unitary parameter.

items.name: Type A half-integral candidates
items.statement: For PGL(n), the dominant adjoint-half-integral generic unitary real parameters are {0} if n is odd and {0, omega_(n/2)/2} if n is even, using the paper numbering.

items.name: Type B half-integral candidates
items.statement: For SO(2n+1), the corresponding set is {0,omega_1/2} in the source root numbering.

items.name: Type C half-integral candidates
items.statement: For PSp(2n), the corresponding set is {0,omega_n/2} in the source root numbering.

items.name: Type D half-integral candidates
items.statement: For PSO(2n), the set is {0,omega_1/2,omega_2/2,omega_n/2} when n is even and {0,omega_n/2} when n is odd, under the source rank conventions.

items.name: Type E7 half-integral candidates
items.statement: For adjoint split E7, the dominant adjoint-half-integral generic unitary region consists of 0 and omega_7/2.

items.name: Other exceptional types
items.statement: For each of split adjoint G2, F4, E6 and E8, the dominant adjoint-half-integral generic unitary region contains only zero.
items.note: A complete extraction must split the four independent root calculations further.

items.name: Testing only the highest weight
items.statement: If nu is half-integral for the adjoint representation, it is half-integral for the irreducible representation of highest weight lambda exactly when <lambda,nu> is in (1/2)Z.

items.name: Fundamental representations exclude nonzero candidates
items.statement: In the respective cases of Proposition 6.31 the displayed fundamental representation pairs with the extra candidate by 1/4, or by 3/4 for E7. For D-type both spin and standard tests are needed to eliminate all candidates.
items.note: Source root numbering and global availability of these representations must be checked; no replacement by the adjoint test alone.

items.name: Local generic temperedness test
items.statement: For split quasi-simple adjoint G and a generic unitary spherical representation, half-integrality of the real part in the adjoint and the specified additional fundamental representations forces the real part to vanish, hence gives temperedness.

items.name: Transfer of the real unitary locus
items.statement: For the unramified nonsplit adjoint groups of Section 7 and real nu fixed by the pinned diagram automorphism tau, the spherical quotients for G and the associated split group G(tau) are unitary, respectively generic unitary, simultaneously.

items.name: Nonsplit generic test with an exclusion
items.statement: For an unramified nonsplit quasi-simple adjoint group other than the quasi-split odd-dimensional PSU group, a generic unitary spherical parameter half-integral in all algebraic representations of the dual semidirect group has zero real part.

items.name: Residual odd-unitary candidate
items.statement: For the excluded odd-dimensional quasi-split unitary group, the argument leaves nu=0 and nu=omega_n/2; the spin representation that excludes the latter for the simply connected fixed dual does not descend to the actual fixed dual SO(2n+1). This is not an automorphic counterexample.

items.name: Generic function-field temperedness
items.statement: Let K be a global function field, G connected absolutely simple over K, and pi cuspidal. Assume pi_v is unramified generic, G at v is unramified quasi-split but not the odd-dimensional quasi-split unitary form, and pi_u is tempered at some place u. Then pi_w is tempered at every place w where pi is unramified and G is unramified quasi-split. Use the coefficient interpretation of Section 4.
items.note: This is the author-v1 statement, not a verified transcription of the 2025 accepted revision.

items.name: Propagation of unramified genericity
items.statement: Under Theorem 5.4, the unramified quasi-split local components in Corollary 5.7 are generic; for globally quasi-split G this holds almost everywhere.

items.name: Kazhdan-Lusztig parameter data
items.statement: For split quasi-simple G, an Iwahori parameter consists of semisimple s, nilpotent e with Ad(s)e=qe, and a Springer-type irreducible representation of the component group of their joint centralizer. Connected-center and general-isogeny classification inputs are distinct.

items.name: Nilpotent partition of the spherical dual
items.statement: Assign to L(s) the nilpotent orbit of the open-orbit raising element in its Aubert-Zelevinsky dual. Define Sph(G,O) and intersect with the unitary dual to obtain CS(G,O). Construct the partition and its normalization at q^(h/2).

items.name: Complementary series from the triple centralizer
items.statement: For O other than 4A1 in E8, if a unitary spherical parameter has real part h/2+nu relative to the reductive triple centralizer, then nu lies in the zero complementary series of the associated centralizer group.

items.name: Extraneous real parameter
items.statement: For a geometric unitary spherical parameter in CS(G,O), its real part is extraneous when it differs from h/2, the central point attached to O.

items.name: Symplectic-dual extraneous parameters
items.statement: For connected-center G with dual Sp(2n), write the nilpotent partition with multiplicities r_i, sum i*r_i=2n and r_i even for odd i. The additional real parameters are h/2+(1/2) sum over even j with r_j>=3 of epsilon_j*omega^j_floor(r_j/2), with epsilon_j in {0,1}, not all zero.
items.note: The proof later prints an odd j where the theorem and centralizer decomposition require even j; resolve against the final version.

items.name: Spin-dual extraneous parameters
items.statement: For connected-center G with dual Spin(n), use the nilpotent partition sum i*r_i=n with r_i even for even i. The additional real parameters are h/2+(1/2) sum over odd i with r_i>=3 of epsilon_i*omega^i_floor(r_i/2), not all epsilon zero, and with sum epsilon_i even.

items.name: Exceptional extraneous-orbit list
items.statement: Under Theorem 8.5 geometricity and connected-center hypotheses, the exceptional orbits admitting additional real parameters are B3 and A1+tilde-A1 in F4; D5(a1)+A1 in E7; and D6, A6, A4+A2, A2+2A1 in E8. There are none in G2 or E6.
items.note: Exact coweight vectors are recorded in the report. Their computation certificates and separate itemization remain completion work.

items.name: Exceptional 4A1 region exclusion
items.statement: For the extra E8,4A1 unitary region in (8.8), the ordered coordinates cannot all lie in (1/2)Z or all in 1/4+(1/2)Z. Thus the extra region contributes no adjoint-half-integral parameter.

items.name: Explicit discrete-spectrum hypotheses
items.statement: For the nongeneric global theorem require a chosen nonzero parameter summand compatible with the unramified Hecke action and local restrictions. In the cuspidal case use the established excursion construction; outside it retain the finite-level rationality and discrete-spectrum decomposition/Satake hypotheses of Section 9 as assumptions.
items.note: The introduction calls the displayed equation Conjecture 9.3. No conjectural assertion is entered here as a proved theorem.

items.name: Conditional rationality of the discrete spectrum
items.statement: Assuming Conjecture 9.1 and the Section 9 coefficient setup, unramified discrete-spectrum Hecke eigenvalues are algebraic and irreducible discrete automorphic representations admit number-field models.
items.note: The two conclusions still need separate items in the completed extraction.

items.name: Representation-indexed weight pattern
items.statement: For a geometric semisimple parameter s, record for every irreducible algebraic representation tau the finitely supported function i |-> multiplicity of weight i among the Frobenius eigenvalues of tau(s).

items.name: Weight patterns determine the real part
items.statement: If two geometric semisimple parameters have identical weight patterns for every algebraic representation, their positive real torus parts are Weyl-conjugate. This does not recover the compact factors.

items.name: Conditional complementary-series propagation
items.statement: In the discrete-spectrum setup of Theorem 1.11, assume an actual compatible global parametrization, a split place v with pi_v in CS(G,N), and a geometric local component at u in S. The source asserts that all split unramified components belong to CS(G,N), with the same central or extraneous real parameter class.
items.note: Review the step from real-part recognition to nilpotent-stratum recognition, as well as the nonadjoint parameter-lifting reduction. This checkpoint does not certify that proof step.

items.name: Boundary and generic weight array
items.statement: For each representation tau, form the finite nonnegative array a(i,j) of Frobenius weight-j multiplicities in the boundary realization of the global weight-i graded piece. Row sums are n_v; column sums are n_u; purity gives a(i,i+j)=a(i,i-j).

items.name: Lexicographic weight comparison
items.statement: Let a:Z x Z -> N have finite support and satisfy a(i,i+j)=a(i,i-j). Set r_i=sum_j a(i,j) and c_i=sum_j a(j,i). Either a is diagonal and r=c, or at the largest index where r and c differ one has c_i>r_i.
items.note: Self-contained combinatorial target. Equality does not follow from symmetry alone.

items.name: Counterexample to automatic equality
items.statement: The array a(0,1)=a(0,-1)=1, zero elsewhere, satisfies the symmetry relation but has row weights concentrated at 0 and column weights at -1 and 1.

items.name: Additional local hypothesis removes extraneous points
items.statement: Under Theorem 1.11, suppose pi_u=AZ(sigma) for an irreducible discrete-series sigma whose pure Weil-Deligne nilpotent operator belongs to the same orbit N as the chosen spherical place. The source concludes that every split unramified real Satake parameter is h_N/2.
items.note: Retain the chosen compatible global parameter and same-orbit hypothesis. Several printed weight comparisons in the proof have n_v on both sides and need independent checking.
